title: Double
body:
`double`. A real number, 8 bytes, roughly 15 significant digits. The default choice for
anything with a decimal point; [[Float]] is the smaller, less precise version and there is
almost never a reason to prefer it. An [[Atomic type]].

```c++
double average = total / count;    // if both are int, this is already wrong
```

That line is the trap. Integer division happens *before* the assignment, so `7 / 2` gives
`3` and then stores `3.0`. Cast one side first: `(double)total / count`. See
[[Type casting]] and [[Division Algorithm]].

Doubles are approximations, so `if (x == 0.1)` is unreliable; compare against a small
tolerance instead. `cout` prints six significant digits by default, which hides the
problem rather than fixing it.
